value: This article defines pure mathematics as the study of abstract mathematical concepts for their intrinsic intellectual challenge and aesthetic value, independent of external applications. While its roots trace back to ancient Greece, the formal distinction from applied mathematics solidified around 1900, driven by the emergence of counter-intuitive theories and a push for greater rigor and axiomatic methods. Despite this, pure mathematics frequently finds unexpected practical uses, blurring the traditional divide, which is now often seen as a philosophical preference rather than a rigid subdivision. A central characteristic is its trend towards increasing generality and abstraction, aiming to deepen understanding and connect different mathematical branches, a pursuit that continues to fuel debate regarding its utility and relationship with the physical world.
